pages.hook: In the USA people love to talk about free time. Learn the words for hobbies, and remember: in the USA, football is not the same sport as in Brazil.

facts.label: What the USA calls futebol
facts.sub: In the USA, “football” usually means American football.

facts.label: Weekend sports
facts.sub: Many children play soccer in a local league on Saturday morning.

facts.label: The Boston Marathon
facts.sub: It is usually held in April in Boston, Massachusetts.

facts.label: Accept an invitation
facts.sub: Also: “Count me in.”

pages.polite: To invite someone, say **Do you want to…?** To accept, say **Sure!** or **I’m in!**

mythfact.s: In the USA, “football” usually means American football.
mythfact.why: The sport with a round ball is called soccer.

mythfact.s: The Boston Marathon is held in April.
mythfact.why: It is usually held in April, on Patriots’ Day (the third Monday of April).

mythfact.s: People in the USA call soccer “football”.
mythfact.why: They call it soccer.

mythfact.s: You can say “I enjoy reading” to talk about a hobby.
mythfact.why: Enjoy + verb-ing is correct.

mythfact.s: The poem “The Swing” was written by Robert Louis Stevenson.
mythfact.why: It was published in 1885 in “A Child’s Garden of Verses”.

decode.q: What time does the game start?

compare.br: In Brazil, futebol is the most popular sport, and people say “jogar bola”.
compare.us: In the USA, baseball, basketball and American football are very popular, and soccer is also played by many children.
compare.tip: Use play with sports and games (play soccer), but with instruments you say play the guitar.
compare.ask: What do you do in your free time? Say two hobbies in English.

quiz.q: A friend asks about your free time. You say…
opts: I play soccer and read books.
I am playing at free time.

quiz.q: You want to invite a friend to play. You say…
opts: Do you want to play soccer on Saturday?
quiz.why: Do you want to… is polite.

quiz.q: A friend invites you. You say yes. You say…
quiz.why: I’m in! = I want to join.

pages.title: Reading quest — My free time in Boston · part 1
text: My name is Jack, and I live in **Boston**. In my free time I play soccer and read books. I **enjoy reading** on the train, and I **enjoy swimming** in the summer.

Last week my friend Grace asked, “What do you do in your free time?” “I play soccer,” I said. “And you?” “I play guitar,” she said. “I’m **into music**.” I asked, “Do you play in a band?” “No, I play at home. Just for fun.”
“Do you want to play soccer on Saturday?” I asked. “Sure! What time?” “At ten, in the park.” “I’m in! **Don’t be late**,” she said, and we both laughed.

fast.why: Jack and Grace talk about free time and plan soccer.

scan.q: What time is the soccer game?

She says, “No, I play at home.”
They play on Saturday.

tf.s: They have lunch after the game.
tf.why: “We played soccer, and then we had lunch.”

On Saturday we played soccer, and then we had lunch. It was a very good morning. What do you do for fun?

pages.title: Reading quest · Talk about it
text: My name is Jack, and I live in **Boston**. In my free time I play soccer and read books. I **enjoy reading** on the train, and I **enjoy swimming** in the summer.

Last week my friend Grace asked, “What do you do in your free time?” “I play soccer,” I said. “And you?” “I play guitar,” she said. “I’m **into music**.” I asked, “Do you play in a band?” “No, I play at home. Just for fun.”
“Do you want to play soccer on Saturday?” I asked. “Sure! What time?” “At ten, in the park.” “I’m in! **Don’t be late**,” she said, and we both laughed.

My favorite poem is “The Swing,” by Robert Louis Stevenson. He wrote it in 1885. In the poem, a child goes up and down on a swing and sees the garden and the river. The child is **having a blast**. I think hobbies are like a swing: they make you happy.
On Saturday we played soccer, and then we had lunch. It was a very good morning. What do you do for fun?
